flood.qualifier: These figures are TERRA's measurement over the products cop30, nasadem, alos, cop90 (Microsoft Planetary Computer). The published range for the study E-hand-flood-baseline used COP30, NASADEM, SRTMGL1 and COP90 from OpenTopography over a single area and does not apply to these figures. HAND is the height of a cell above the drainage cell it flows to. It is not a hydrodynamic model: rainfall, discharge, routing and channel geometry are not modelled. A threshold in metres ranks relative susceptibility; it is not a flood depth, extent or probability. Disagreement between products indicates cells where the result depends on the choice of DEM.

assumptions.drainage_threshold: A cell is drainage when at least 0.5 km2 drains through it, which is 585 cells at this cell size. This is the study's reference value. The extent moves with this value, which is held fixed here; its contribution to the reported disagreement is unmeasured.
assumptions.reference_threshold: The agreement raster is built at HAND <= 1.0 m. The study reports its widest disagreement between products at 1 m.
assumptions.thresholds: Thresholds swept: [1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0] m. These are the values the study reports.
assumptions.reporting_extent: Every count, area, fraction and IoU here is taken over the 5256 cells inside the AOI polygon, 4.495 km2. The terrain chain ran over 43848 cells, 37.5 km2, since HAND requires the contributing area upstream of the AOI. That window is reported under grid and buffer_m as provenance; no figure here is measured over it. A cell is counted when its centre falls inside the polygon, so the reported area differs from the polygon's own area by at most half a cell along the boundary.
assumptions.inset_margin: The inset statistics repeat every comparison over the AOI shrunk by 18 cells, about 501 m, measured from the AOI boundary and covering 1332 cells. The ring is cut from the AOI polygon. Near the AOI boundary the contributing area does not include drainage from beyond the buffer, so HAND reads high and the extent small. A large gap between iou and iou_inset indicates that the disagreement is concentrated near that boundary. The default 1000 m ring is 36 cells on this grid and was capped at 18, which leaves at least half the shorter side of the AOI bounding box inside the inset.
assumptions.cell_size: Cells are 27.9 by 30.7 m, evaluated at the centre latitude of the window (hand.pixel_size_m). Areas in this payload are cell counts multiplied by that cell area; no projected-area calculation is applied.
assumptions.alignment: All products are on one grid. A product whose native grid differs was aligned by nearest neighbour and is marked resampled in its row. Its disagreement with the others carries an alignment component in addition to the terrain difference. A null in that column means the caller did not report whether the product was resampled.
assumptions.buffer: The DEM was read 2000 m beyond the AOI, so the drainage entering the AOI is measured terrain. Drainage arriving from beyond that buffer is absent, which biases HAND high and the extent low near the AOI edge. The chain ran over the buffered window; the figures are taken over the AOI.
excluded: No rainfall, discharge, routing or hydrodynamic simulation.
No observed flood: nothing here is compared against a satellite or gauge record of an event.

No channel bathymetry, levees, dams or drainage infrastructure. The measured surface is the DEM surface, which over open water is the water surface at acquisition and, for products that are not bare earth, includes buildings and canopy.

No vertical datum harmonisation between products. HAND is a height difference within one product, so a constant offset between products cancels. A spatially varying offset does not cancel and appears here as terrain disagreement.
No uncertainty from the drainage threshold, which is held fixed.
No temporal dimension: the products were acquired years apart and the terrain is treated as unchanged between them.
assumptions.rasters: The GeoTIFF holds the agreement counts over the whole computed 216 by 203 window, buffer included, on the grid the grid block describes. The PNG holds the same counts clipped to the AOI: a 73 by 72 cell bounding box with every cell outside the polygon transparent, placed by extent. That is the ground the figures are measured over.
assumptions.chain_grid: The terrain chain ran on the shared 216 by 203 grid for every product. A product whose native cells are coarser was moved onto that grid before the chain. The other order, the chain on the native grid and the resulting mask aligned after, gives a different extent for such a product: measured over one 6 by 6 km window (n=1), the two orders agreed at IoU 0.47 for COP90 at the 1 m threshold and at 0.95 for a product already at 30 m. Pairs flagged resampled carry a method component of that order in addition to the terrain difference. Pairs flagged false carry the terrain difference alone.
